data.gender_notes: Dakshil is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Dakshil is derived from the Sanskrit word 'daksh' meaning 'skilled' or 'expert'. In Hindu mythology, Daksha Prajapati is a renowned sage and father of many gods and goddesses. The name Dakshil embodies the spirit of proficiency and mastery, inspiring confidence and respect. The name Dakshil carries the meaning “Skilled, Expert, Adept” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Dakshil usually hope their child will grow to embody skilled, expert, adept and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: The name 'Dakshina' is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Dakshina' which means 'southern'. It was used to refer to the southern parts of India, especially the Deccan region. Historically, it was also the name of the ancient Indian kingdom located in the southern part of the Indian subcontinent, which is now known as the Andhra Pradesh and Telangana regions. This kingdom existed during the 2nd century BCE to the 3rd century CE.
historical_references.context: Ancient Indian kingdom in the Deccan region

historical_references.reference: Dakshina or Dakshina Murti is also the name of Lord Shiva in Hinduism, who is depicted as having received the third eye from the goddess Sati. The name 'Dakshina' in this context refers to 'the receiver of the oblations' or 'the one who receives the offerings'. This form of Lord Shiva is believed to bestow his devotees with wealth and prosperity. This reference is from the Hindu Puranas, which are ancient religious texts of Hinduism.
